title: Multi-Cloud Certificate Expiry Tracking

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.4.31 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.4.31 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`aws:acm:inventory` collected via ACM/Key Vault/Certificate Manager exports, optional certstream; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: Expired certs break TLS for APIs and VPNs across regions; a unified expiry calendar prevents outages.
value: Detecting multi-cloud certificate expiry tracking early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Nightly inventory jobs push cert metadata via HEC. Escalate at 30, 14, and 7 days. Include private CAs and cloud-managed certs for load balancers and API gateways.

knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure ACM/Key Vault/Certificate Manager exports, optional certstream with the modular input for `aws:acm:inventory`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Nightly inventory jobs push cert metadata via HEC. Escalate at 30, 14, and 7 days. Include private CAs and cloud-managed certs for load balancers and API gateways.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:acm:inventory" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:acm:inventory" ( OR sourcetype="azure:keyvault:certs" OR sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.31_multi_cloud_certificate_31"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:acm:inventory` in `index=cloud` to detect multi-cloud certificate expiry tracking. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_31_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Table (cert, provider, days left), Timeline (expiry dates), Single value (next expiry)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade ACM/Key Vault/Certificate Manager exports, optional certstream and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of multi-cloud certificate expiry tracking so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
